name: Motion (formerly Framer Motion) + Motion+
one_liner: Production-grade open-source animation library for React, JavaScript and Vue, with a paid Motion+ toolkit.
what_it_offers: MIT-licensed animation library (npm `motion`, v13.2.0) covering springs, gestures (hover/press/drag), layout and shared-element animations, AnimatePresence exit animations, scroll-linked animation, timelines and motion values. Motion+ adds 450+ copy-paste examples, a premium API library (Ticker, Carousel, AnimateNumber, Cursor, Typewriter, ScrambleText, splitText, Curtains), Motion UI (30 animated site sections such as heroes, pricing, navigation, testimonials and page transitions, installable through shadcn), 110+ tutorials, a visual transition editor for IDEs, and the AI Kit (MCP server, /motion best-practice skill, MotionScore performance audits, CSS spring generation).
tech_stack: TypeScript; packages for React (motion/react), vanilla JS and Vue (motion-v); hybrid JS + WAAPI/ScrollTimeline engine
portfolio_fit_reason: The default motion layer for React/Next.js portfolios: page transitions, scroll reveals, shared-element project-card-to-case-study transitions and micro-interactions, free under MIT and very agent-friendly.
client_ok_note: Core library is MIT; the Motion+ FAQ says its APIs and examples are MIT too. Personal licence covers one person; teams need Business seats.
best_use_for_portfolio: Use layout and shared-element animations so a project thumbnail expands smoothly into its case-study page, add scroll-linked reveals for case-study sections, and spring hover states on project cards. Motion+ Ticker or splitText suits a client-logo marquee or an animated name headline.
tier_reason: The default motion layer for React and Next.js portfolios: page transitions, scroll reveals, shared-element card-to-case-study transitions. MIT and highly agent-friendly.
pick_over_overlaps: Use it for component state, layout and exit animations in React. Pair it with GSAP for long scroll timelines rather than forcing one to do both. Skip Motion+ unless you want the AI Kit or Motion UI sections.
score_rationale: The default animation layer for React/Next.js sites. It is free, MIT, actively released and very agent-friendly (llms.txt, MCP, shadcn). Motion+ adds ready-made animated sections and examples that directly raise the polish of a distinctive site, for a one-time $399 for a solo developer.
free_tier: The full core Motion library (MIT, open source), all public docs, a basics set of examples and tutorials, and free AI Kit docs search (no token or account needed). Motion+ is required for the /motion best-practice skill, examples search, MotionScore, CSS spring generation, the transition editor, Motion UI and shadcn install, premium APIs (AnimateNumber, Carousel, Cursor, Ticker, Typewriter, ScrambleText, splitText, Curtains), the full 450+ examples and 110+ tutorials, and the private GitHub/Discord.
paid_entry_label: Motion+ Personal $399 one-time with lifetime updates, for a single user (US checkout on 2026-09-14 showed $399.00 USD total before tax; PPP pricing shows a local discount in some currencies). There is no monthly plan.
paid_top_label: Motion+ Business $249/seat/year (annual subscription, minimum 2 seats, transferable seats; e.g. 5 seats = $1,245/yr + tax). The Builder's License for products that resell Motion+ capabilities has no public price (contact sales).
commercial_use_license: The core library is MIT (GitHub LICENSE.md, npm license field). The Motion+ FAQ says its APIs and examples are also MIT-licensed, so code added to your site is yours and can be used in commercial projects. Personal is a single-user licence, and the FAQ says use by more than one person requires Business seats. If your product effectively resells Motion+ capabilities to your users, you need a separate Builder's License. The FAQ's 'see above' points to no visible section on /plus, and the AI Kit SDK docs say to contact Motion (via X) about it for externally facing tooling, so its terms and price are unpublished. A 'builders' value of 4999 (USD) appears in the site's public pricing API (api.motion.dev/pricing/v2), but it is not displayed or described as an offer.
agent_friendly: Very strong. npm package `motion`; llms.txt at motion.dev/llms.txt indexing the docs; AI Kit plugin with its own MCP server (one-click for Cursor, install guide for Claude Code and Codex). Docs search is free; the examples MCP/search, /motion skill, MotionScore and CSS springs are paid. Motion UI sections install through the shadcn CLI from a private registry.
maintenance_signal: GitHub motiondivision/motion: ~33.6k stars, MIT, last push 2026-09-13. npm motion v13.2.0 published 2026-09-02. About 15.4M weekly downloads for `motion` plus ~34.3M for `framer-motion` (2026-09-05 to 09-11). README sponsors include Framer (partner), Cursor, Linear, Figma and Sanity.
caveats: The premium layer is a paid one-time purchase for solo use. Teams need annual per-seat Business licences (minimum 2 seats), and products that resell Motion+ capabilities need a Builder's License with no public price or terms. The page's JSON-LD (£299 GBP) is a hardcoded fallback in the site code, not the live price. The live pricing API and US Stripe checkout both show $399 USD. PPP and student discounts are available on request by email. The React bundle is heavier than CSS-only animation unless you use LazyMotion. The 14-day refund is void once GitHub is linked or source is accessed. Some things that look basic (splitText, agent best-practice skill) are Motion+ only.
unverified_fields: Builder's License price and terms (not published; the pricing API's 'builders: 4999' USD value is not presented as an offer)
Size of PPP and student discounts (issued case by case via support@motion.dev)

comparables.why: Industry-standard timeline/scroll animation engine (ScrollTrigger, SplitText, MorphSVG), framework-agnostic. Free for commercial use under GSAP's own no-charge Standard License, not MIT.

comparables.name: React Spring
comparables.why: Spring-physics animation library for React (pmndrs, ~29k GitHub stars); an open-source alternative for natural motion.

comparables.why: MIT, open-source copy-paste animated React + Tailwind components built on Motion, a free counterpart to Motion UI.
